purpose: machine-usable ontology for understanding and appraising how news is produced and how the media system works: production craft and verification, news values and framing, media business models and distribution, and bias and slant, yielding calibrated credibility judgments.
assumptions: this KB is a subdomain node in a knowledge-searcher meta-KB about where and how to find, retrieve, evaluate, and synthesize authoritative knowledge
nodes are concrete, evaluable work-units for appraising how news works, not a newsroom production manual
no observed dataset is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
appraisal targets range over a single item, an outlet, or the surrounding media system as scoped per analysis
exclusions: disinformation campaign attribution and influence-operations forensics
audience reception measurement and survey methodology
newsroom HR, advertising sales operations, and production tooling

competency_questions.question: What exactly is being appraised about this news item or outlet, and which genre standard applies?
Is this item hard-news reporting, opinion, analysis, or sponsored content?
Does the report establish the five Ws and how, and are any core facts missing or unattributed?
How is each claim sourced, and does the sourcing support the weight of the claim?
Which claims are verified, plausible, or unverified, and was the item corrected if wrong?
Why did this event become news, and which comparably important events were not covered?
Where in the editorial and platform pipeline was information filtered, and what was filtered out?
How does coverage volume and placement shape which issues seem important?
How is the story framed, and how would an alternative frame change the read?
Where is bias entering: through omission and selection, word-level slant, or both?
Is the story's balance appropriate or does it manufacture false equivalence?
What is the outlet's revenue model and ownership, and what editorial incentives do they create?
How do attention/engagement incentives and platform distribution shape what gets produced?
What is the calibrated credibility verdict, with what uncertainty and what would change it?

glossary.definition: the who, what, when, where, why (and how) a report should establish
the editorial and platform filtering that decides which events and sources enter coverage
media influence on which issues audiences judge important via coverage volume and placement
the selection and emphasis that defines a problem, cause, evaluation, and remedy in a story
bias from which facts, sources, and stories are included or left out
directional bias in word choice, labeling, tone, and headline framing within an item
presenting fringe and well-evidenced positions as equivalent
competition for finite audience attention that drives engagement-optimized content
independent confirmation of a claim from a separate source or document
the criteria (timeliness, proximity, impact, conflict, novelty) that make events newsworthy

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from journalism-studies and media-systems literature (Kovach & Rosenstiel 'The Elements of Journalism'; Schudson; Gans 'Deciding What's News'; McCombs & Shaw agenda-setting; Entman framing; Hallin & Mancini media systems) and analytic practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Fix the question being answered about a news item or outlet and the appraisal purpose (understand, verify, attribute, or compare) before any sourcing or judgment.
contradictors: reader who treats every article identically
inputs: news item or outlet under question

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: clarifies what 'evaluate this news' even means
pros.example: clarifies what 'evaluate this news' even means

pros.claim: prevents scope creep into unrelated outlet history
pros.example: prevents scope creep into unrelated outlet history

cons.claim: an over-narrow scope hides systemic context
cons.example: an over-narrow scope hides systemic context

failure_modes: confusing 'is it true' with 'is it biased'
appraising a system from one article
acceptance_tests: scope question is answerable from the item itself
revisit_triggers: item turns out to be part of a larger campaign

nodes.definition: Distinguish hard news reporting from opinion, analysis, sponsored content, press release, and entertainment so the right appraisal standard is applied.

included: news vs opinion vs native ad split

contradictors: reader who reads opinion as straight news

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: opinion and native ads carry different truth obligations than reporting
pros.example: opinion and native ads carry different truth obligations than reporting

cons.claim: hybrid formats (analysis) resist clean labels
cons.example: hybrid formats (analysis) resist clean labels

failure_modes: treating a column as a news report
acceptance_tests: genre label assigned with cited signal

nodes.definition: Check that a report establishes who, what, when, where, why, and how, and flag which core facts are missing, hedged, or unattributed.
contradictors: reader satisfied by a vivid lede alone

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: exposes reports that lead with color but omit the core facts
pros.example: exposes reports that lead with color but omit the core facts

cons.claim: a complete five-Ws can still be false or slanted
cons.example: a complete five-Ws can still be false or slanted

acceptance_tests: each W mapped to a sentence or marked missing
revisit_triggers: a missing W is later supplied by a correction

nodes.definition: Identify each claim's source, its attribution status (named, anonymous, documentary, single, or multiple), and whether sourcing supports the weight of the claim.
contradictors: reader who trusts 'sources say' uncritically

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: anonymous-source-heavy claims are weaker and need extra scrutiny
pros.example: anonymous-source-heavy claims are weaker and need extra scrutiny

pros.claim: multi-sourcing raises confidence
pros.example: multi-sourcing raises confidence

cons.claim: legitimate whistleblowers require anonymity, so anonymity is not automatically a defect
cons.example: legitimate whistleblowers require anonymity, so anonymity is not automatically a defect

failure_modes: accepting a single anonymous source for an extraordinary claim
missing that 'reports' cites another outlet, not original reporting
acceptance_tests: every load-bearing claim has an identified source or is flagged

nodes.definition: Test factual claims against independent evidence, prior reporting, primary documents, and corroborating sources, separating verified, plausible, and unverified claims.
contradictors: reader who equates publication with verification

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: independent corroboration is the discipline that separates journalism from rumor
pros.example: independent corroboration is the discipline that separates journalism from rumor

cons.claim: full verification is slow and sometimes impossible under deadline
cons.example: full verification is slow and sometimes impossible under deadline

failure_modes: treating repetition across outlets as corroboration
acceptance_tests: each claim labeled verified/plausible/unverified with basis
revisit_triggers: a verified claim is later debunked

nodes.definition: Assess whether the outlet has transparent correction, retraction, and accountability practices and whether the specific item was corrected or stands uncorrected.
contradictors: outlet that silently edits without disclosure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: a visible corrections culture is a strong positive credibility signal
pros.example: a visible corrections culture is a strong positive credibility signal

cons.claim: absence of corrections may mean either accuracy or opacity
cons.example: absence of corrections may mean either accuracy or opacity

acceptance_tests: correction status of the item determined

nodes.definition: Explain why an event became news using news-value criteria (timeliness, proximity, prominence, impact, conflict, novelty, human interest) and what comparably important non-events were not covered.
contradictors: reader who assumes coverage equals importance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: explains why some true important events get no coverage at all
pros.example: explains why some true important events get no coverage at all

cons.claim: news values are descriptive, not a justification for distortion
cons.example: news values are descriptive, not a justification for distortion

failure_modes: treating high news value as high importance
acceptance_tests: at least one comparable uncovered event named

nodes.definition: Trace how editors, wire services, platforms, and routines filter which events and sources pass into coverage, and where information was filtered out.
contradictors: reader who sees the news as a neutral mirror

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: locates the structural choke points where coverage is shaped
pros.example: locates the structural choke points where coverage is shaped

cons.claim: gatekeeping is harder to observe than published output
cons.example: gatekeeping is harder to observe than published output

acceptance_tests: at least one gate identified with mechanism
revisit_triggers: a gate is bypassed by direct publishing

nodes.definition: Assess how coverage volume and placement shape which issues audiences think are important (first-level) and which attributes of those issues are emphasized (second-level).

excluded: the directional slant of each story

contradictors: reader who thinks placement is arbitrary

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: explains issue salience without assuming any factual error
pros.example: explains issue salience without assuming any factual error

cons.claim: agenda-setting effects are probabilistic and audience-dependent
cons.example: agenda-setting effects are probabilistic and audience-dependent

nodes.definition: Identify how a story is framed (problem definition, causal attribution, moral evaluation, recommended remedy, episodic vs thematic) and how alternative frames would change the read.
contradictors: reader who sees framing as merely 'spin'

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: reveals how true facts can still steer interpretation via frame choice
pros.example: reveals how true facts can still steer interpretation via frame choice

cons.claim: frame identification is interpretive and can over-read intent
cons.example: frame identification is interpretive and can over-read intent

failure_modes: labeling any framing as deliberate bias
missing episodic framing that hides systemic causes
acceptance_tests: all four frame functions addressed or marked absent
at least one alternative frame articulated
revisit_triggers: frame analysis couples into slant detection

nodes.definition: Detect bias arising from which facts, sources, and stories are included or omitted, distinct from biased wording within an item.
contradictors: reader who only checks for loaded words

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: captures the most consequential bias, which is usually omission not wording
pros.example: captures the most consequential bias, which is usually omission not wording

cons.claim: proving omission requires a baseline of what should have been covered
cons.example: proving omission requires a baseline of what should have been covered

acceptance_tests: omitted material specified against a baseline

nodes.definition: Detect partisan or directional slant in word choice, labeling, tone, headline-body mismatch, and loaded quotation selection within a single item.
contradictors: reader who thinks neutral tone equals neutral story

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: catches directional labeling and headline clickbait that the body does not support
pros.example: catches directional labeling and headline clickbait that the body does not support

cons.claim: word-level slant is the least consequential and most over-weighted bias
cons.example: word-level slant is the least consequential and most over-weighted bias

acceptance_tests: each slant flag cites specific wording

nodes.definition: Decide whether a story's balance is appropriate or whether it manufactures false equivalence between well-evidenced and fringe positions.
contradictors: editor enforcing symmetric 'both sides' regardless of evidence

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: distinguishes fair balance from evidence-blind false equivalence
pros.example: distinguishes fair balance from evidence-blind false equivalence

cons.claim: judging 'fringe' requires evidence assessment that can itself be contested
cons.example: judging 'fringe' requires evidence assessment that can itself be contested

failure_modes: calling a real dispute false balance
platforming a fringe view as one of two equals
acceptance_tests: evidence weight of each side stated
false-equivalence calls reference the verification ledger

nodes.definition: Map the outlet's revenue model (advertising, subscription, donor/nonprofit, public funding, attention/engagement) and the editorial incentives each model creates.
contradictors: reader who ignores who pays for the news

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: revenue model predicts systematic editorial pressures
pros.example: revenue model predicts systematic editorial pressures

cons.claim: incentive does not prove a specific story was distorted
cons.example: incentive does not prove a specific story was distorted

acceptance_tests: at least one concrete incentive risk named

nodes.definition: Analyze how competition for attention and engagement metrics drives clickbait, outrage, virality optimization, and pace over depth.
contradictors: reader who treats virality as merit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: explains structural pressure toward outrage and speed over accuracy
pros.example: explains structural pressure toward outrage and speed over accuracy

cons.claim: engagement optimization is not unique to low-quality outlets
cons.example: engagement optimization is not unique to low-quality outlets

failure_modes: treating all popular content as clickbait
acceptance_tests: engagement incentive linked to observable content choices
revisit_triggers: outlet shifts to subscriptions reducing engagement pressure

nodes.definition: Assess how platform algorithms, search, and aggregators mediate reach and how distribution incentives reshape headlines, format, and what gets produced.
contradictors: reader who assumes readers come directly to outlets

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: explains why headline/format choices serve algorithms, not just readers
pros.example: explains why headline/format choices serve algorithms, not just readers

cons.claim: platform internals are opaque, so effects are inferred
cons.example: platform internals are opaque, so effects are inferred

failure_modes: over-attributing all format choices to algorithms

nodes.definition: Identify who owns and funds the outlet, ownership concentration, and the editorial-independence safeguards or pressures ownership creates.
contradictors: reader who ignores ownership entirely

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: ownership and funding are upstream of many editorial pressures
pros.example: ownership and funding are upstream of many editorial pressures

cons.claim: ownership influence is real but not deterministic for any single story
cons.example: ownership influence is real but not deterministic for any single story

failure_modes: inferring story distortion directly from owner identity

nodes.definition: Characterize an outlet's partisan or ideological positioning across stories using consistent slant and selection patterns, not a single article.
contradictors: reader who labels an outlet from one headline

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: a multi-story estimate is far more reliable than a one-article label
pros.example: a multi-story estimate is far more reliable than a one-article label

cons.claim: positioning estimates can entrench reader priors and be gamed
cons.example: positioning estimates can entrench reader priors and be gamed

failure_modes: labeling an outlet from a small or cherry-picked sample
acceptance_tests: estimate based on a stated sample size

nodes.definition: Integrate verification, framing, bias, and systemic findings into a calibrated credibility judgment for the item or outlet, with explicit uncertainty and what would change it.
contradictors: reader wanting a binary trustworthy/untrustworthy label

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: forces a calibrated, uncertainty-aware verdict instead of a label
pros.example: forces a calibrated, uncertainty-aware verdict instead of a label

cons.claim: premature synthesis before verification locks an unreliable verdict
cons.example: premature synthesis before verification locks an unreliable verdict

failure_modes: collapsing nuance into a binary score
weighting word slant over omission and verification
revisit_triggers: a correction or new evidence appears

nodes.definition: Produce a reusable, auditable record of the appraisal: findings, evidence trail, residual uncertainties, and revisit triggers for the next reader or session.
contradictors: reader who keeps no trail

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new evidence, correction, or expanded sample materially shifts this finding

pros.claim: makes the appraisal reproducible and revisable as facts change
pros.example: makes the appraisal reproducible and revisable as facts change

cons.claim: a record can imply more finality than the evidence supports
cons.example: a record can imply more finality than the evidence supports

failure_modes: recording a verdict without its evidence trail

edges.why_related: genre discrimination needs the appraisal purpose fixed first
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scoped purpose tells which genre standard matters
edges.risk_of_conflict: typing genre before scope wastes effort
edges.example: decide 'verify vs compare' before judging genre

edges.why_related: completeness standard depends on whether item is reporting or opinion
edges.benefit_of_coupling: correct genre sets the right completeness bar
edges.risk_of_conflict: applying news bar to an op-ed misjudges it
edges.example: apply five-Ws only to reporting

edges.why_related: sourcing is checked against the core facts the report claims
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the fact inventory tells which claims need sources
edges.risk_of_conflict: sourcing without a claim inventory misses gaps
edges.example: map each W to its source

edges.why_related: verification operates on the identified sources of each claim
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a source map directs corroboration effort
edges.risk_of_conflict: verifying before sourcing is unfocused
edges.example: corroborate the named/anonymous sources found

edges.why_related: correction status is meaningful relative to what was verified or debunked
edges.benefit_of_coupling: verified errors map to expected corrections
edges.risk_of_conflict: judging corrections without verification is empty
edges.example: check if debunked claims were corrected

edges.why_related: newsworthiness analysis applies to reporting, set by genre
edges.benefit_of_coupling: genre frames which selection norms apply
edges.risk_of_conflict: analyzing values of an ad misleads
edges.example: explain why a hard-news event was covered

edges.why_related: gatekeeping explains how news-value events are filtered into coverage
edges.benefit_of_coupling: value profile sets the baseline for what passed gates
edges.risk_of_conflict: gatekeeping without value baseline is unanchored
edges.example: trace which valued events were filtered out

edges.why_related: salience effects follow from what gatekeeping let through
edges.benefit_of_coupling: gate map grounds the salience read
edges.risk_of_conflict: salience claims without gatekeeping are speculative
edges.example: measure salience of issues that passed gates

edges.why_related: framing analyzes how salient issues are presented
edges.benefit_of_coupling: salience tells which issues to frame-check
edges.risk_of_conflict: framing without salience context misranks effort
edges.example: frame the issues the agenda elevated

edges.why_related: word-level slant is read within the established frame
edges.benefit_of_coupling: frame identifies where slant would live
edges.risk_of_conflict: slant scanning without a frame is noisy
edges.example: check loaded labels inside the chosen frame

edges.why_related: omission bias is assessed against the frame and its alternatives
edges.benefit_of_coupling: frame contrast exposes omitted material
edges.risk_of_conflict: omission claims need a frame baseline
edges.example: name facts the frame omitted

edges.why_related: selection bias is grounded in the gatekeeping map
edges.benefit_of_coupling: gate map shows where selection skew enters
edges.risk_of_conflict: selection bias without gatekeeping is assertion
edges.example: tie omitted stories to specific gates

edges.why_related: false-balance judgment needs the evidence weight from verification
edges.benefit_of_coupling: verified evidence weight distinguishes real vs false balance
edges.risk_of_conflict: calling false balance without evidence is itself biased
edges.example: weigh sides by verified evidence

edges.why_related: balance is judged within the framing of the controversy
edges.benefit_of_coupling: frame shows how the controversy is staged
edges.risk_of_conflict: balance without frame misses manufactured controversy
edges.example: detect a frame that invents a two-sided debate

edges.why_related: systemic analysis is scoped by the appraisal purpose
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scope decides whether outlet economics are in view
edges.risk_of_conflict: analyzing economics off-scope wastes effort
edges.example: include revenue model only when appraising the outlet

edges.why_related: attention dynamics are a property of the revenue model
edges.benefit_of_coupling: revenue mix sets the engagement pressure
edges.risk_of_conflict: analyzing attention without the model is shallow
edges.example: trace outrage incentives to ad/engagement revenue

edges.why_related: platform distribution amplifies attention incentives
edges.benefit_of_coupling: engagement pressure explains platform-driven format
edges.risk_of_conflict: platform effects without attention context are partial
edges.example: link headline format to algorithmic reach

edges.why_related: ownership and funding sit upstream of the revenue model
edges.benefit_of_coupling: revenue profile points to who funds it
edges.risk_of_conflict: ownership read without funding context is thin
edges.example: connect funder dependence to ownership

edges.why_related: outlet positioning aggregates per-item selection findings
edges.benefit_of_coupling: selection findings feed the cross-story estimate
edges.risk_of_conflict: positioning without per-item findings is a guess
edges.example: aggregate omission patterns across stories

edges.why_related: positioning aggregates per-item slant findings
edges.benefit_of_coupling: slant findings feed the positioning estimate
edges.risk_of_conflict: positioning from one item's slant is unreliable
edges.example: require a multi-story slant sample

edges.why_related: the verdict integrates the verification ledger
edges.benefit_of_coupling: verified facts anchor the credibility judgment
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthesizing before verification locks an unreliable verdict
edges.example: weight verified vs unverified claims in the verdict

edges.why_related: the verdict accounts for selection and omission bias
edges.benefit_of_coupling: omission findings shape the credibility read
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring omission inflates the verdict
edges.example: fold omission findings into the verdict

edges.why_related: the verdict reflects whether balance was fair or false
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balance verdict adjusts credibility
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping balance distorts the verdict
edges.example: note false-equivalence in the verdict

edges.why_related: the verdict considers ownership-driven independence risk
edges.benefit_of_coupling: ownership context calibrates the verdict
edges.risk_of_conflict: systemic risk omitted understates pressure
edges.example: record independence risk in the verdict

edges.why_related: the verdict situates the item in outlet positioning
edges.benefit_of_coupling: positioning contextualizes the item
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring positioning misreads a one-off
edges.example: contextualize the item by outlet positioning

edges.why_related: the audit record documents the synthesized verdict
edges.benefit_of_coupling: verdict supplies the record's core
edges.risk_of_conflict: recording before synthesis captures nothing
edges.example: write the record after the verdict

edges.why_related: revenue incentives change which stories and sources are selected
edges.benefit_of_coupling: exposes economic drivers of selection skew
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-attributing selection to economics
edges.example: ad-dependence suppressing advertiser-critical coverage
edges.resolution_rule: treat as influence, verify against actual coverage

edges.why_related: engagement optimization changes the probability of loaded headlines and tone
edges.benefit_of_coupling: links outrage tone to engagement pressure
edges.risk_of_conflict: assuming all strong tone is engagement-driven
edges.example: clickbait headline overstating the body
edges.resolution_rule: attribute to incentive only with content evidence

edges.why_related: algorithmic format pressure changes how completely facts are presented
edges.benefit_of_coupling: flags platform-driven truncation of core facts
edges.risk_of_conflict: blaming algorithms for all incompleteness
edges.example: a thread optimized for reach dropping the 'why'
edges.resolution_rule: weigh platform pressure against editorial choice

edges.why_related: ownership and funding change the probability of a partisan editorial line
edges.benefit_of_coupling: connects positioning to ownership pressure
edges.risk_of_conflict: inferring positioning purely from ownership
edges.example: owner's politics correlating with the editorial line
edges.resolution_rule: require output evidence, not owner identity alone

edges.why_related: thorough verification competes with speed and engagement incentives
edges.benefit_of_coupling: names the speed-vs-accuracy tradeoff
edges.risk_of_conflict: sacrificing verification for a faster post
edges.example: breaking-news race publishing unverified claims
edges.resolution_rule: accuracy dominates; mark unverified explicitly, never publish-as-fact

edges.why_related: demanding named multi-sourcing can conflict with protecting legitimate anonymous sources
edges.benefit_of_coupling: surfaces the anonymity-vs-corroboration tension
edges.risk_of_conflict: rejecting a true claim solely for anonymity
edges.example: whistleblower account that cannot be on-record
edges.resolution_rule: require independent corroboration, allow justified anonymity

edges.why_related: calling out false balance can look partisan and feed positioning disputes
edges.benefit_of_coupling: exposes the balance-vs-neutrality-perception tension
edges.risk_of_conflict: labeling evidence-based calls as partisan
edges.example: correcting a fringe-vs-consensus framing being called biased
edges.resolution_rule: ground calls in the verification ledger, not partisan priors

edges.why_related: legitimate news values and biased omission both reduce coverage of some events
edges.benefit_of_coupling: separates editorial judgment from bias
edges.risk_of_conflict: branding all low-coverage as bias
edges.example: an unglamorous but important policy story going uncovered
edges.resolution_rule: distinguish news-value rationale from systematic skew

edges.why_related: the verdict must not over-weight easily-spotted word slant over omission and verification
edges.benefit_of_coupling: guards against slant-dominated verdicts
edges.risk_of_conflict: scoring an outlet low for tone while ignoring accuracy
edges.example: a strongly-worded but accurate and complete report
edges.resolution_rule: weight verification and omission above word slant

edges.why_related: a later correction triggers re-verification of the affected claim
edges.benefit_of_coupling: keeps the ledger current with corrections
edges.risk_of_conflict: looping endlessly on minor edits
edges.example: outlet issues a correction reversing a key fact
edges.resolution_rule: revisit only on material corrections; stop when ledger re-stabilizes

edges.why_related: a fired revisit trigger sends the verdict back for update
edges.benefit_of_coupling: re-opens the verdict when conditions change
edges.risk_of_conflict: re-opening on immaterial changes
edges.example: a registered trigger (new evidence) fires
edges.resolution_rule: revisit only when a trigger materially fires; stop at a stable verdict

edges.why_related: a positioning estimate flags items to re-audit for selection bias
edges.benefit_of_coupling: focuses re-audit on suspicious items
edges.risk_of_conflict: confirmation-driven re-auditing
edges.example: positioning suggests systematic single-side sourcing
edges.resolution_rule: re-audit a bounded sample; stop when the pattern is confirmed or refuted

edges.why_related: omission and framing both shape interpretation without altering individual facts
edges.benefit_of_coupling: helps deduplicate interpretive-bias checks
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating omission with framing
edges.example: both can make a true story misleading
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct: framing=presentation, omission=what is left out

edges.why_related: the verdict reflects the outlet's corrections behavior
edges.benefit_of_coupling: accountability practice calibrates the verdict
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring corrections culture overstates trust
edges.example: credit a transparent corrections record

conflict_axes.trigger: breaking-news and engagement pressure push publication before verification is complete
resolution_order: mark unverified claims as unverified
never present unverified as fact
publish only what is corroborated or clearly labeled
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: accuracy dominates speed; speed never licenses presenting unverified claims as established fact
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an extraordinary unverified claim is about to be published as fact under deadline
conflict_axes.example: a viral 'breaking' claim later retracted after the race to publish

conflict_axes.trigger: appraisers fixate on loaded words while the larger bias is what was omitted
resolution_order: audit omission against a coverage baseline first
then assess word-level slant
weight omission above wording in the verdict
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: omission and selection analysis dominates word-level slant when they conflict in the verdict
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an outlet is scored mainly on tone while major omissions go unexamined
conflict_axes.example: a tonally neutral report that omits the decisive counter-evidence

conflict_axes.trigger: a both-sides norm presents fringe and well-evidenced positions as equals
resolution_order: weigh each side by verified evidence
reject symmetric treatment when evidence is asymmetric
report the evidentiary asymmetry explicitly
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: evidence weight dominates a symmetric balance norm; balance follows the evidence, not vice versa
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a manufactured controversy is staged as a legitimate two-sided debate
conflict_axes.example: giving equal time to a well-supported finding and a fringe denial

conflict_axes.trigger: characterizing an outlet's intent risks unfair attribution versus naming real systematic skew
resolution_order: describe observable patterns, not motives
require a multi-item sample before attributing positioning
record uncertainty
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: observable-pattern evidence dominates motive attribution; never infer intent from a single item
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a partisan label is applied from one headline or a cherry-picked sample
conflict_axes.example: branding an outlet from a single unrepresentative story

conflict_axes.trigger: economic and ownership incentives suggest distortion that a specific story may not show
resolution_order: treat incentives as priors, not proof
require content evidence before claiming a story was distorted
report incentive risk separately from story findings
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: story-level evidence dominates incentive inference for claims about a specific item
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an item is judged distorted purely because the owner has an interest
conflict_axes.example: assuming advertiser pressure altered a story with no content evidence

conflict_axes.trigger: maintaining privileged source access can compromise independent scrutiny of those sources
resolution_order: disclose access relationships
corroborate access-dependent claims independently
flag access-driven framing
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: independence dominates access; access never substitutes for independent corroboration
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a beat reporter softens coverage to protect a key source relationship
conflict_axes.example: official-source access shaping coverage to keep the access

conflict_axes.trigger: protecting legitimate anonymous sources conflicts with the demand for named, corroborable sourcing
resolution_order: allow anonymity only with justification
require independent corroboration of anonymous claims
escalate single-anonymous-source extraordinary claims
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: corroboration dominates: anonymity is permitted but never excuses lack of independent support
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a single anonymous source carries an extraordinary unsupported claim
conflict_axes.example: a whistleblower account that must stay anonymous yet needs corroboration

conflict_axes.trigger: legitimate editorial news judgment and biased omission both reduce coverage of some events
resolution_order: state the news-value rationale
compare to a coverage baseline
label as bias only on a systematic pattern
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: a systematic skew pattern dominates a single low-coverage instance when calling something bias
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: every low-coverage topic is branded as deliberate bias
conflict_axes.example: an unglamorous but important story uncovered for news-value, not bias, reasons

conflict_axes.trigger: readers want a simple trustworthy/untrustworthy label that erases real uncertainty
resolution_order: report a calibrated verdict with uncertainty
state what would change the verdict
avoid collapsing to a binary score
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: calibrated uncertainty-aware synthesis dominates a binary label
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a single trust score is demanded that hides material uncertainty
conflict_axes.example: collapsing a nuanced mixed record into one number

edge_cases.trigger: an unverified claim is treated as verified in the verdict
edge_cases.example: a deadline claim entered the verdict as fact without corroboration
edge_cases.detection_method: check that every claim in the verdict has a verified/plausible/unverified label

edge_cases.trigger: repetition of a claim across outlets is counted as independent corroboration
edge_cases.example: three outlets all citing the same single original source
edge_cases.detection_method: trace each citation to its original source; flag shared origin

edge_cases.trigger: appraisal scores only word slant and ignores omission
edge_cases.example: a tonally neutral piece that omits decisive counter-evidence
edge_cases.detection_method: require an omission audit against a baseline before a slant-only verdict

edge_cases.trigger: an outlet is labeled partisan from a single article
edge_cases.example: calling an outlet biased from one headline
edge_cases.detection_method: require a stated multi-item sample size before positioning

edge_cases.trigger: an opinion column or native ad is appraised as hard news
edge_cases.example: a sponsored post evaluated for newsroom completeness
edge_cases.detection_method: check section labels and disclosure before applying the news standard

edge_cases.trigger: a genuine dispute is wrongly called false balance, or fringe is platformed as equal
edge_cases.failure_mode: balance verdict error in either direction
edge_cases.example: labeling a real scientific debate as false balance
edge_cases.detection_method: tie every false-equivalence call to the verification ledger

edge_cases.trigger: a story is judged distorted from ownership/economic incentive alone
edge_cases.example: declaring a story biased because the owner has an interest
edge_cases.detection_method: require content evidence before attributing distortion to incentive
resolution: separate incentive risk from story finding

edge_cases.trigger: synthesis is finalized before verification is reviewed
edge_cases.example: writing the verdict before the verification ledger is complete
edge_cases.detection_method: check workflow order and must_not_finalize_before constraints

edge_cases.trigger: a verdict is reused after a correction or new evidence
edge_cases.example: citing an old verdict after the story was corrected
edge_cases.detection_method: check revisit triggers against the record's timestamp

edge_cases.trigger: platform-optimized format drops core facts but is read as complete
edge_cases.example: a social thread optimized for reach that omits the 'why'
edge_cases.detection_method: compare the distributed version against the full report

edge_cases.trigger: a metric is labeled observed though no dataset exists
edge_cases.example: tagging a heuristic sourcing score as observed
edge_cases.detection_method: scan metric_labels and value_labels for observed/experimentally_validated

workflow.objective: fix the appraisal question and the applicable genre standard
entry_criteria: a news item or outlet is supplied
acceptance_tests: scope question answerable from the item
genre assigned with a cited signal
workflow.do_first_because: nothing downstream is valid until the question and the applicable standard are fixed

workflow.objective: inventory the core facts and map each claim to its sourcing
acceptance_tests: each W mapped or marked missing
every load-bearing claim has an identified source or flag
workflow.do_first_because: verification and bias work need the fact and source inventory first

workflow.objective: verify claims against independent evidence and check correction status
workflow.do_first_because: the credibility verdict cannot precede the verification ledger

workflow.objective: explain why the event is news and trace where information was filtered
acceptance_tests: at least one gate identified with mechanism
workflow.do_first_because: selection context is needed before agenda and framing effects can be read

workflow.objective: assess issue salience and the framing of the story
acceptance_tests: all frame functions addressed or marked absent
workflow.do_first_because: framing and salience must precede bias detection that builds on them

workflow.objective: detect omission, word-level slant, and false-balance bias
workflow.do_first_because: item-level bias findings feed outlet positioning and the verdict

workflow.objective: map revenue model, attention incentives, distribution, and ownership
workflow.do_first_because: systemic incentives contextualize item findings and must be kept separate from story-level proof

workflow.objective: estimate outlet positioning from aggregated multi-item findings
acceptance_tests: estimate based on a stated sample
workflow.do_first_because: positioning needs aggregated item findings and must not be drawn from one item

workflow.objective: integrate findings into a calibrated verdict and produce an audit record
acceptance_tests: human review recorded for high-risk verdict
workflow.do_first_because: the verdict integrates everything and must not be locked before verification and bias review pass

dominance_rules.rule: verification dominates speed; unverified claims are never presented as fact
dominance_rules.required_action: mark unverified explicitly and withhold fact-status until corroborated
dominance_rules.example: holding a breaking claim until independently corroborated

dominance_rules.trigger: a verdict could be driven by word slant over omission
dominance_rules.rule: omission and selection bias dominate word-level slant in the verdict
dominance_rules.required_action: weight omission and verification above tone when scoring
dominance_rules.example: not downgrading an accurate, complete report for strong wording

dominance_rules.trigger: a both-sides norm conflicts with asymmetric evidence
dominance_rules.rule: evidence weight dominates symmetric balance; report the asymmetry
dominance_rules.required_action: weigh sides by verified evidence and state any asymmetry
dominance_rules.example: refusing equal time to a fringe denial against a well-supported finding

dominance_rules.trigger: incentive inference conflicts with story-level evidence
dominance_rules.rule: story-level content evidence dominates incentive inference for claims about an item
dominance_rules.required_action: require content evidence before attributing distortion to incentives
dominance_rules.example: separating ownership-incentive risk from the actual story finding

dominance_rules.trigger: positioning is being inferred from one item
dominance_rules.rule: a multi-item pattern dominates single-item inference for outlet positioning
dominance_rules.required_action: require a stated sample and uncertainty band before labeling
dominance_rules.example: refusing to brand an outlet from one unrepresentative story

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk verdict tempts a fast unreviewed finalization
dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates speed; high-risk nodes require human review
dominance_rules.required_action: route risk_if_wrong>=0.80 nodes to human review before lock
dominance_rules.example: holding the final verdict for review when stakes are high

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is tempting to do before its prerequisites
dominance_rules.required_action: do not finalize a node before its prerequisites are reviewed
dominance_rules.example: not writing the verdict before the verification ledger exists

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible attribution or distortion call arises
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible or contested calls
dominance_rules.required_action: escalate anonymous-source claims, distortion and false-balance calls
dominance_rules.example: human sign-off before publishing a distortion attribution

dominance_rules.trigger: a metric is tempting to label observed for confidence
dominance_rules.required_action: keep heuristic labels and zero observed fields absent a dataset
dominance_rules.example: leaving sourcing scores heuristic rather than claiming observed

dominance_rules.trigger: a verdict or finding lacks a traceable basis
dominance_rules.required_action: tie every finding and verdict to evidence_refs and the ledger
dominance_rules.example: rejecting a credibility claim that cites no underlying finding

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix scope and genre before any appraisal work
anti_rework_rules.rationale: wrong scope or standard invalidates all downstream findings
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: findings later redone after the question changes
anti_rework_rules.example: applying a news standard to an op-ed

anti_rework_rules.rule: classify genre before applying the completeness standard
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: completeness re-judged after a genre correction

anti_rework_rules.rule: inventory the core facts before mapping sourcing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: sourcing without a claim inventory misses gaps
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: source map redone after missing claims surface
anti_rework_rules.example: mapping sources before listing the claims

anti_rework_rules.rationale: verification is unfocused without a source map
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: verification redirected after sources are mapped
anti_rework_rules.example: verifying before knowing who said it

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete verification before the credibility verdict
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a verdict on unverified claims is unreliable
anti_rework_rules.example: scoring credibility before the ledger exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: analyze selection and gatekeeping before agenda and framing effects
anti_rework_rules.rationale: effects without a selection baseline are unanchored
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: effects reanalyzed after selection is mapped
anti_rework_rules.example: claiming salience effects with no gatekeeping context

anti_rework_rules.rule: establish framing before omission and slant detection
anti_rework_rules.rationale: bias findings need a frame baseline
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: bias findings redone after the frame is set
anti_rework_rules.example: scanning slant before identifying the frame

anti_rework_rules.rule: aggregate item-level findings before estimating positioning
anti_rework_rules.rationale: positioning from one item is unreliable
anti_rework_rules.example: labeling an outlet before gathering a sample

anti_rework_rules.rule: require acceptance tests and human review before locking high-risk verdicts
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking before tests/review causes irreversible error
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a locked verdict reopened after review finds a flaw
anti_rework_rules.example: publishing a verdict before human sign-off

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank by risk and downstream impact
action: score defects by risk and coupling
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents and edges from the node
acceptance_tests: all dependents of a changed node identified

iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to a repair subsystem
acceptance_tests: each defect routed to exactly one owner

iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator and formula script

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or a correction arrives
iteration_protocol.detection: compare new posterior to prior beyond delta
acceptance_tests: posterior change exceeds revisit delta before re-locking

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible call is open
further iteration yields no material gain
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no material improvement across two passes

checks.repair_action: modeled accuracy/speed and incentive tensions as conflict edges, not dependencies
recomputed all derived fields via formula script

change_triggers: a claim is verified or debunked
the outlet changes revenue model or distribution

increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
human_approval_required_for: hard lock of the credibility verdict
